mainTopic: Who is kept from the קרבן פסח and from holy food: the ערל, the בן נכר, the אונן, and a baby not yet due for מילה
overview: This amud finishes explaining the extra words in the פסח פסוקים. The word בו teaches that a משומד is kept from the קרבן פסח but not from מעשר, and that a ערל is kept from the פסח but still eats מצה and מרור. The גמרא explains why the תורה had to mention both the ערל and the בן נכר, and says the two words ממנו are needed for a teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק. Next it looks at רבי עקיבא, who learns from "איש איש" that a ערל may not eat holy food. The גמרא asks why that phrase includes the ערל and not the אונן, and decides for ערלות, either because it has more reasons or, as רבא says, because "איש" points to something found only in men. The גמרא then shows what each תנא does with "תושב ושכיר" and "איש איש". Finally, רב חמא בר עוקבא asks whether a baby too young for מילה counts as a ערל for oil of תרומה. רבי זירא tries to prove it from a ברייתא about the קרבן פסח, but רבא pushes the proof aside, and the back-and-forth continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Being a משומד disqualifies from the פסח but not from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer about the word בו in the פסוק of בן נכר: being a משומד keeps someone from the קרבן פסח, but not from eating מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'from it' teaches that apostasy disqualifies a person from the Paschal lamb, but apostasy does not disqualify a person from eating tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began just before this line. The word בו ('from it') limits the rule about the בן נכר to the קרבן פסח alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, בן נכר means a Jew who has turned away from ה׳, a משומד. The word בו shows that his disqualification applies only to the קרבן פסח. So a משומד may still eat מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a משומד, a Jew who has abandoned the תורה
Disqualifies
Tithe (here, food holy enough to need a restriction)
A 'stranger,' here a Jew estranged from ה׳

phrases.english: Apostasy disqualifies,
but apostasy does not disqualify regarding tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשׁוּמָּדוּת פּוֹסֶלֶת, וְאֵין מְשׁוּמָּדוּת פּוֹסֶלֶת בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question (asked just before this line) about why בו is written regarding בן נכר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו limits the disqualification of a משומד to the קרבן פסח and excludes מעשר.

steps.title: Why does the verse about the uncircumcised say 'from it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word בו adds in the פסוק 'כל ערל לא יאכל בו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'No uncircumcised person shall eat from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about a different פסוק. What does the extra word בו teach in the פסוק about the ערל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בו in the בן נכר פסוק has just been used for a teaching. The ערל פסוק also says בו, so it too must be limiting something. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
Why do I need it? (asking what an extra word teaches)

phrases.english: "No uncircumcised person shall eat from it"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כׇּל עָרֵל לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question about the word בו to the ערל פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word בו excludes in the פסוק about the ערל.

steps.title: The ערל still eats מצה and מרור
steps.stepSummary: בו teaches that a ערל is kept only from the קרבן פסח. He still eats מצה and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not eat from it, the Paschal lamb, but he does eat matza and bitter herbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בו limits the ערל's restriction to the קרבן פסח alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without בו, we might think a ערל is kept from all the פסח-night מצוות. The word בו teaches that he is still obligated in מצה and מרור like every other Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread eaten on פסח night
Bitter herbs eaten on פסח night

steps.whatToRemember: The word בו shows up for both the בן נכר and the ערל. In each case it limits the disqualification to the קרבן פסח only (not מעשר, not מצה and מרור).

phrases.english: From it he does not eat,
but he does eat matza and bitter herbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל, אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא בְּמַצָּה וּמָרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו excludes מצה and מרור. A ערל is barred only from the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: Why the תורה needed to mention both the ערל and the בן נכר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ערל and the בן נכר could not be learned from each other, because each has a different reason for being disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah needed to write 'uncircumcised' and also 'any stranger.' Had it written only 'uncircumcised,' I would say that is because his state is repulsive, but a stranger, who is not repulsive, might be allowed. Had it written only 'any stranger,' I would say that is because his heart is not directed to Heaven, but an uncircumcised man, whose heart is directed to Heaven, might be allowed. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question nobody asked out loud: why does the תורה need two separate פסוקים? It shows that each case has its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ערל is disqualified because his condition is repulsive (מאיס), and that reason does not apply to a בן נכר. A בן נכר is disqualified because his heart is not toward Heaven, and that reason does not apply to a ערל who wants to serve ה׳. Each reason fits only one case, so neither could be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
The Merciful One (ה׳, as author of the תורה)
Repulsive
His heart is directed toward Heaven
It is necessary (both are needed)

steps.confusionAlert: The ערל here is not a sinner. He wants to do the מצוה but could not (for example, because of danger). That is why the גמרא says his heart is toward Heaven.
steps.whatToRemember: This is a classic צריכותא: two similar laws, each needed, because each has its own reason that does not carry over to the other.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "uncircumcised,"
and it was necessary to write "any stranger."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:43

phrases.english: For if the Merciful One had written only "uncircumcised,"
I would say it is because he is repulsive.
But a stranger, who is not repulsive —
I might say he is not prohibited.
And if the Merciful One had written only "any stranger,"
I would say it is because his heart is not toward Heaven,
but an uncircumcised man, whose heart is toward Heaven —
I might say he is not prohibited,
so both are necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״עָרֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״כׇּל בֶּן נֵכָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having discussed both פסוקים, the גמרא justifies why both are written.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason, so neither can be learned from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Write only ערל, and a בן נכר might be allowed, since he is not repulsive. Write only בן נכר, and a ערל might be allowed, since his heart is toward Heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both פסוקים are needed, and both the ערל and the בן נכר are barred from the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: Why does the Torah say 'of it' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the word ממנו appears twice in the פסוקים about the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of it,' 'of it': why do I need these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to two more limiting words, ממנו and ממנו, in the פסח פסוקים and asks what they teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like בו, the word ממנו sounds like it is limiting something. The גמרא asks what each one comes to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: Of it (a limiting word)

phrases.english: "Of it," "of it": why do I need them?
phrases.notes: שמות 12:9 and שמות 12:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בו to another limiting word, ממנו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the two occurrences of ממנו teach.

steps.title: Needed for the teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The two words ממנו are needed for a teaching that רבה said in the name of רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are needed for what רבה said in the name of רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly: these words are already used for a teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ממנו are not available for some new limitation because they are already used for that teaching. The גמרא only names the source here and does not spell the teaching out.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which רבה said

phrases.english: For that which Rabba said that Rabbi Yitzchak said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two words ממנו are used for the teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the ערל from "איש איש"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא from the ברייתא. He says the doubled words "איש איש" teach that a ערל may not eat holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי עקיבא says it is not needed, because the פסוק says "איש איש", and that comes to include the ערל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא so it can look at it more closely. It is setting up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not need any other source for the ערל. The פסוק could have said "איש" once, but it says it twice. He reads the extra word as adding the ערל to the people who may not eat holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the גמרא is quoting a line from a source it brought earlier, so it can discuss it
"A man, a man": a doubled word in the פסוק, read as including more people
To include, to add something to the law
A man who is not circumcised

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Akiva says: It is not needed,
phrases.notes: He means we don't need the other source the ברייתא used for the ערל.

phrases.english: for it says "any man" [literally: a man, a man],
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

phrases.english: to include the uncircumcised man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a new line in the ברייתא to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the doubled "איש איש" includes a ערל in the ban on eating holy food.

steps.title: Maybe the extra word includes an אונן instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why "איש איש" should not include an אונן instead of a ערל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it comes to include the אונן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's reading. It suggests that the extra word might be talking about an אונן, not a ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word tells us that someone is included, but it does not say who. So the גמרא asks how we know the added person is the ערל and not the אונן.

keyTerms.meaning: "But say": the גמרא offers a different way to read the source
A person whose close relative has died and has not yet been buried

phrases.english: But say: to include the acute mourner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which person the extra word in step 7 includes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's use of "איש איש" to include the ערל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word only shows that someone is added. It could just as easily be the אונן.

steps.title: "וכל זר": strangeness keeps a person out, mourning does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers from "וכל זר". The Torah keeps out a stranger, not a mourner, so an אונן may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: the פסוק says "וכל זר", meaning: I told you that being a stranger keeps you out, not being a mourner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Another פסוק shows that an אונן is not kept from eating, so "איש איש" cannot be about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זר points to זרות, being an outsider, as the reason a person cannot eat. Mourning is a different kind of problem. So the פסוק excludes the אונן, and the extra word is left to include someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A stranger, someone who is not a כהן
Being a stranger or outsider
The state of being an אונן, a mourner before the burial

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
The verse says: "And no stranger"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10

phrases.english: Being a stranger, I told you, [keeps one out],
and not acute mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכׇל זָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate פסוק excludes the other option
steps.terutzMaskana: "וכל זר" excludes the אונן, so "איש איש" must include the ערל.

steps.title: Maybe "וכל זר" also excludes the ערל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the same פסוק means only strangeness keeps someone out, and not uncircumcision either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: and not uncircumcision!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי יוסי's reading around. It asks whether "וכל זר" might also leave out the ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If זר means only being an outsider matters, then a ערל, who is a full כהן, should also be allowed to eat. The answer from step 9 now seems to cut against the ערל too.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of not being circumcised
"Say": the גמרא suggests a different reading

phrases.english: Say: and not lack of circumcision?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 9 by using the same logic on the ערל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of "וכל זר" in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only זרות keeps someone out, then ערלות should not keep a כהן out either.

steps.title: "איש איש" already includes the ערל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that "איש איש" is written, and it includes the ערל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written "איש איש"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ערל cannot be left out, because "איש איש" brings him in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two פסוקים work together. "וכל זר" leaves out the אונן, and "איש איש" brings in the ערל. That way neither פסוק is wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it is written": pointing to a פסוק that settles the question

phrases.english: But it is written: "any man" [a man, a man].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to the פסוק that includes the ערל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכל זר" might leave out the ערל.
steps.terutzMaskana: "איש איש" includes the ערל, so only the אונן is left out.

steps.title: Why choose the ערל over the אונן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made us decide that "איש איש" includes the ערל and "וכל זר" leaves out the אונן, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we split the two פסוקים this way. It is setting up a comparison between ערלות and אנינות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק includes someone and one leaves someone out, but the words alone don't say who is who. We need a reason why the ערל is the one included.

keyTerms.meaning: "And what did you see?": what reason made you choose this way and not the opposite?

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why include the ערל and leave out the אונן, rather than the reverse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way steps 9 and 11 divided the two פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for including the ערל and excluding the אונן, rather than the reverse.

steps.title: Five reasons ערלות is more serious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives five reasons why ערלות is more serious and so is the better one to include. It uses a memory list: מעשים, כרותים, בדבר, העבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to include ערלות. A ערל is missing an action, and that action is on his body. Not doing it is punished with כרת. מילה was commanded before the תורה was given. And not circumcising one's sons and slaves holds a person back from eating the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ערלות is the more serious problem, so it is the one the extra word includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the more serious problem should be the one that keeps a person from eating holy food. Each of the five points shows that ערלות is heavier. The memory list gives one key word per point, and "מעשים" stands for the first two points.

keyTerms.meaning: "It makes sense": an answer based on reasoning
A heavenly punishment of being cut off
Before the Torah was given at Sinai
Holds back, stops something from happening

phrases.english: It makes sense that lack of circumcision
is the one he should include,
for: Acts, Karetim, Word, the Slave.
phrases.notes: This is a memory list for the reasons that come next. "Acts" covers the first two.

phrases.english: He is missing an action,
and the action is on his body,
and it is punished with karet,
and it existed before the Divine Speech,
phrases.notes: מילה was already commanded to אברהם, long before מתן תורה.

phrases.english: and the circumcision of his males and slaves holds [him] back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערלות is more serious in five ways, so it is the one that should be included.

steps.title: On the contrary: אנינות seems more serious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite. אנינות can happen at any time, it applies to men and women, and the mourner cannot fix it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! אנינות should be the one included. It can happen at any time, it applies to men and women, and it is not in a person's power to fix himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 13. It gives three reasons why the אונן might be the better one to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the more serious problem should be included. Now the גמרא shows that אנינות has serious features too. It can strike anyone at any moment, it covers both men and women, and the mourner cannot end it by himself. So the choice is not settled yet.

keyTerms.meaning: "On the contrary": arguing the exact opposite
It is not in his power to fix his own situation

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא is weighing ערלות against אנינות to decide which one "איש איש" includes. Each side has its own reasons. Steps 15 and 16 settle it in favor of ערלות.

phrases.english: On the contrary:
acute mourning is the one he should include,
for it can happen at any time,
and it applies to men and women,
and it is not in his hands to fix himself!
phrases.notes: A ערל can fix himself by having a ברית מילה. An אונן has to wait for the burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against the reasoning in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that ערלות is the better one to include
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אנינות has its own serious features, so it could be the one that is included.

steps.title: The reasons for including the ערל are more numerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 14. There are more reasons that make ערלות serious than reasons that make אנינות serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-back from the last step. It says the five reasons for ערלות outnumber the three reasons for אנינות, so ערלות is still the better one to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 gave three reasons why אנינות might be more serious. The answer does not argue with those three reasons. It just says the five reasons on the ערלות side are more in number, so "איש איש" should include the ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: those, these (pointing back to the reasons just listed)
are more numerous, there are more of them

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "These" means the five reasons for ערלות from step 13. They outnumber the three reasons for אנינות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by counting the reasons on each side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing by number: more reasons on one side decide the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three reasons for אנינות might show that אונן is the one included by "איש איש".
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערלות side has more reasons, so the ערל is the one included.

steps.title: רבא: "איש איש" points to something found only in men
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a stronger answer. Even without counting reasons, "איש איש" stresses a man, and the only one of the two that applies only to men is ערלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without the point that these reasons are more numerous, you cannot say otherwise. The verse says "איש איש" (a man, a man). What is something that applies to a man and not to a woman? You must say it is ערלות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer that does not need any counting. He reads the words of the פסוק themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "איש" means a man, so the inclusion must be about something found only in men. ערלות only applies to men, but step 14 said אנינות applies to both men and women. So "איש איש" cannot be including the אונן, and it must be including the ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: without
you cannot say (the other side)
you must say, this has to be
being uncircumcised

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why "איש איש" includes the ערל: there are more reasons for ערלות, and (רבא) the word "איש" points to something found only in men.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without "these are more numerous,"
you cannot say it (the other way around).
The verse says, "a man, a man,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

phrases.english: what is something that applies to a man
and does not apply to a woman?
You must say: this is uncircumcision.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָא הָנָךְ נְפִישָׁן נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, stronger answer to step 14, based on the wording of the פסוק and not on counting reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the פסוק: the word "איש" limits it to men.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אנינות has its own strong reasons, maybe "איש איש" includes the אונן.
steps.terutzMaskana: "איש" points to something found only in men, and that is ערלות. אנינות applies to women too, so it is not included.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא learn from "תושב ושכיר"?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא learns ערל from "איש איש", the גמרא asks what he does with the words "תושב ושכיר" said about the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, what does he do with this phrase "a sojourner and a hired worker"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks what the words "תושב ושכיר" teach according to רבי עקיבא, and this sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, the words "תושב ושכיר" were used by the other view to teach about the ערל. רבי עקיבא already learns the ערל from "איש איש", so he does not need these words for that. The גמרא wants to know what they teach him instead, because a פסוק's words are not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: a sojourner and a hired worker (words in the פסוק about the קרבן פסח)
what does he do with it, what does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,
this phrase "a sojourner and a hired worker,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:45

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הַאי ״תּוֹשָׁב וְשָׂכִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי עקיבא's source for the ערל is settled, the גמרא asks what his view does with the other פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי עקיבא learns from the words "תושב ושכיר", since he does not need them for the ערל.

steps.title: רב שמעיה: to include a circumcised Arab or Gibeonite
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה says the words teach that a circumcised Arab or a circumcised Gibeonite may not eat the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: It comes to include a circumcised Arab and a circumcised Gibeonite.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה gives a first answer. The words "תושב ושכיר" teach that even a non-Jew who is circumcised still cannot eat the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some non-Jewish peoples did circumcise. We might think that once they are circumcised they are no longer kept out. רב שמעיה says the extra words teach that they are still kept out.

keyTerms.meaning: to include, to bring in another case
a circumcised Arab
a Gibeonite

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
To include a circumcised Arab
and a circumcised Gibeonite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמַעְיָא: לְאֵתוֹיֵי עַרְבִי מָהוּל וְגִבְעוֹנִי מָהוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "תושב ושכיר" teaches that a circumcised Arab or Gibeonite is still not allowed to eat the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: A משנה shows non-Jews never count as circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שמעיה. A משנה about vows shows that circumcised non-Jews are treated as uncircumcised, so a פסוק is not needed to keep them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these considered circumcised? But we learned in a משנה: If someone says "Any benefit I get from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me like a קונם," he may benefit from uncircumcised Jews and may not benefit from circumcised non-Jews. If he says "Any benefit I get from the circumcised is forbidden to me like a קונם," he may benefit from circumcised non-Jews and may not benefit from uncircumcised Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שמעיה's answer. It brings a משנה showing that a non-Jew is called "uncircumcised" even if he had a ברית, so of course he is kept out like any ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, "uncircumcised" means non-Jews and "circumcised" means Jews, no matter what was done to the body. So a circumcised Arab is still an ערל in the eyes of הלכה. There is no need for extra words to keep him out of the קרבן פסח, so רב שמעיה's answer does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn in a משנה?
a word used in vows to make something forbidden like a קרבן
gets benefit
the nations of the world, non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, "circumcised" and "uncircumcised" are names for Jews and non-Jews, not a description of the body. That is why a circumcised non-Jew counts as "uncircumcised".

phrases.english: And are these considered circumcised?
But didn't we learn:
"Benefit I get from the uncircumcised is קונם (forbidden) to me":
he is allowed to benefit from uncircumcised Jews,
and forbidden to benefit from circumcised non-Jews.
"Benefit I get from the circumcised is קונם (forbidden) to me":
he is allowed to benefit from circumcised non-Jews,
and forbidden to benefit from uncircumcised Jews!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב שמעיה's answer from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמעיה's claim that "תושב ושכיר" is needed to keep out a circumcised Arab or Gibeonite.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in נדרים shows that a circumcised non-Jew still counts as uncircumcised. So he is already kept out as an ערל, and the words cannot be needed for him.

steps.title: New answer: a convert who did not immerse, and a baby born circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב שמעיה's answer. "תושב ושכיר" keeps out a convert who was circumcised but did not yet immerse, and a baby born without a foreskin, because רבי עקיבא holds such a baby still needs דם ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to include a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse, and a baby who was born already circumcised. And רבי עקיבא holds that one must draw a drop of covenant blood from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of step 17. It names two people who look circumcised but are still missing something, and says the words keep them out of the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The convert had his ברית מילה but has not finished converting until he goes in the מקוה. The baby born without a foreskin still needs a drop of דם ברית, and רבי עקיבא holds this is required. Until then, neither one may eat the קרבן פסח, and that is what "תושב ושכיר" teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
a convert who was circumcised but did not yet immerse
a baby born without a foreskin
he holds, his opinion is
to draw a drop of covenant blood

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, "תושב ושכיר" keeps out people who look circumcised but are not yet complete: a convert before טבילה, and a baby born circumcised before הטפת דם ברית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that רבי עקיבא holds a baby born without a foreskin still needs הטפת דם ברית, which is a real halachic position on how such a child enters the ברית.

phrases.english: Rather, to include a convert
who was circumcised but did not immerse,
and a baby who was born circumcised.
And he holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: one must draw from him a drop of covenant blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי גֵּר שֶׁמָּל וְלֹא טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב שמעיה's answer, which step 19 knocked down, with a new answer to step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the answer: the words are about different people.
steps.terutzMaskana: "תושב ושכיר" keeps out a convert before טבילה and a baby born circumcised before הטפת דם ברית, since רבי עקיבא holds that this is needed.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר does not need 'תושב ושכיר' to exclude anyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not need the words 'תושב ושכיר' to exclude the two cases רבי עקיבא excludes. In his view, a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse is a full convert, and a baby born without a foreskin needs no דם ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning. He said that a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse is a proper convert. He also holds that a baby born circumcised does not need covenant blood drawn from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר is free to use 'תושב ושכיר' for a גזירה שוה. For him, there is nothing left for those words to exclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבי עקיבא used 'תושב ושכיר' to keep out two people: a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse, and a baby born without a foreskin. רבי אליעזר holds that both of these people are already fully fit. So for him, the words are not needed to exclude anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with a view he holds elsewhere
A convert who was circumcised but did not immerse in a מקוה
A proper, full convert
To draw a drop of covenant blood

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: He uses 'תושב ושכיר' for a גזירה שוה, so the גמרא shows why he doesn't need those words to exclude anyone.

phrases.english: as he said: a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse
is a proper convert,
and he holds: a child who was born circumcised

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַטִּיף מִמֶּנּוּ דַּם בְּרִית.
phrases.english: does not need to have covenant blood dripped from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 20 and shows that רבי אליעזר disagrees with both cases that רבי עקיבא excluded.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with the opinion's known views elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי אליעזר also needs 'תושב ושכיר' to exclude these cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר both cases are already fit, so the words are free for a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר do with 'איש איש'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר explains the doubled words 'איש איש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with this phrase 'איש איש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר learns from the repeated word 'איש איש'. רבי עקיבא used it to teach about ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a doubled word in the תורה is read as teaching something extra. Since רבי אליעזר does not learn ערל from it, the גמרא wants to know what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?
Literally 'a man, a man', a doubled word in the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
this phrase "any man [ish ish]," what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אִישׁ אִישׁ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from 'תושב ושכיר' to the other key phrase, 'איש איש', and asks about it according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from the doubled 'איש איש'

steps.title: The תורה speaks like people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that 'איש איש' is ordinary speech, so no extra law is learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר does not learn anything from the doubled word. People normally talk that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds the rule of דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם. A doubled word like 'איש איש' is just normal style and is not an extra hint. רבי אליעזר does not need it for the ערל anyway, because he learns that a ערל may not eat holy food from the גזירה שוה of 'תושב ושכיר' (see step 21).

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke the way people normally speak, so extra words are not always read for a new law

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns ערל from 'איש איש'. רבי אליעזר reads it as normal speech, because he holds דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No special law is learned from 'איש איש', because it is ordinary speech.

steps.title: May a baby not yet circumcised be anointed with oil of תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר עוקבא asks whether a baby who is too young to be circumcised counts as an ערל for oil of תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר עוקבא asked: May we anoint an uncircumcised baby with oil of תרומה? Does being uncircumcised before the right time hold him back, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Is a baby who is not circumcised yet, only because he is not eight days old, treated like an ערל when it comes to תרומה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערל may not eat תרומה. But this baby is not circumcised only because his time for מילה has not come yet. The question is whether his lack of circumcision still counts, or only counts once the מצוה applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question, raised a dilemma
To anoint him (with oil)
Oil that is תרומה, the holy portion given to a כהן
Being uncircumcised before the time when מילה is required
Holds back, disqualifies

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Ukva raised a dilemma:
an uncircumcised child, what is the law
about anointing him with oil of teruma?
Does lack of circumcision not at its time disqualify,
phrases.notes: 'Not at its time' means before the eighth day, when the baby isn't supposed to be circumcised yet.

phrases.english: or does it not disqualify?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the theme of ערל and holy things.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether being uncircumcised before the time of מילה disqualifies a baby from benefiting from תרומה

steps.title: רבי זירא begins a proof from the ברייתא about sons and slaves at the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא. It teaches that circumcision of sons and of slaves holds a person back both when the פסח is slaughtered and when it is eaten, learned through a גזירה שוה of 'אז' and 'אז'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Come and hear. I would only know about circumcising one's sons at the time of slaughtering the פסח, and one's slaves at the time of eating it. How do we know to apply what was said about each case to the other? The פסוק says 'אז' and 'אז' for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts bringing a ברייתא to answer רב חמא בר עוקבא's question. This line sets up the proof, which the גמרא develops next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the פסוק mentions sons' circumcision at the slaughter and slaves' circumcision at the eating. The word 'אז' (then) appears in both places, so each rule is applied to the other. רבי זירא will use this ברייתא to show something about a baby who is not yet circumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, an introduction to a proof
At the time of preparing, meaning slaughtering, the קרבן פסח
At the time of eating the קרבן פסח
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִילַת זְכָרָיו בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּה,
phrases.english: I have only the circumcision of his males at the time of preparation,
phrases.notes: 'Preparation' here means slaughtering the קרבן פסח. שמות 12:48.

phrases.english: and of his slaves at the time of eating.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what was said about this one to that one,
and what was said about that one to this one?
The verse states "then" and "then" for a verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer the question raised in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב חמא בר עוקבא's question about a baby who is not yet circumcised and oil of תרומה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא linking circumcision of sons and slaves at the slaughter and the eating of the פסח through the גזירה שוה of 'אז'

steps.title: A newborn between slaughter and eating seems to prove that early ערלות counts
steps.stepSummary: Slaves can join the household between שחיטה and eating if they are bought then. Sons can only join that way by being born then. So the ברייתא seems to prove that ערלות שלא בזמנה is still ערלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: With slaves it makes sense: he could buy them after the slaughter and before the eating. But with sons, how could they be there at eating time and not at slaughter time? Only if they were born in between. So a baby who is not yet due for מילה still counts as uncircumcised!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא from step 25 and tries to use it to answer רב חמא בר עוקבא's question from step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that sons and slaves hold back the eating of the פסח even if they did not hold back the slaughter. For slaves, the case is simple: they were bought in between. For sons, the only case that comes to mind is a baby born in between, who is far from his eighth day. So even an ערלות that is not yet due would count as ערלות.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (opens a contrast: 'this is fine, but...')
The time of preparing the פסח, meaning its slaughter
The time of eating the פסח, at night
In between
Being uncircumcised before the time for מילה has come

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about grown sons. It is about a baby who could not have a ברית yet because he is less than eight days old.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would answer רב חמא בר עוקבא's question: a baby too young for מילה would count as an ערל.

phrases.english: It works out well regarding his slaves:
you can find a case where they are there at the time of eating
but were not there at the time of preparation,
for example, where he bought them in between.
But his males (his sons),
who are there at the time of eating
but were not there at the time of preparation,
how can you find such a case?
Is it not where they were born between the preparation and the eating?
phrases.notes: A newborn can't have his ברית until the eighth day, so this baby is nowhere near his time yet.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
being uncircumcised before its time still counts as being uncircumcised!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 25 to answer the question of step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That ערלות שלא בזמנה counts as ערלות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that sons hold back the eating even when they did not hold back the slaughter

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the פסוק ties eating the פסח to circumcising males first. A baby who cannot be circumcised yet cannot hold anyone back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How can you think that? The תורה says 'Let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and offer it.' This baby is not fit for מילה yet!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof from step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says: circumcise your males, and then bring the פסח. That only makes sense for a male who can be circumcised now. A newborn who is not yet fit for מילה cannot be part of that requirement, so he cannot stop his father from eating.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (opens a rejection)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Fit to be circumcised

phrases.english: רבא said: And can you really think so?
The Torah says: "Let all his males be circumcised,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48

phrases.english: "and then let him come near and offer it."
And this baby is not fit for circumcision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim that a newborn not yet due for מילה holds back the פסח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק only connects the פסח to a male who can be circumcised now.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a baby whose fever went away
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא differently: a baby who was sick at slaughter time and got better before eating time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? For example, a baby whose fever left him.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the proof, רבא gives another way to read the ברייתא's case of sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At slaughter time the baby was sick, so he could not be circumcised and did not hold anyone back. By eating time the fever was gone, so he was now fit for מילה and could hold his father back. This keeps the ברייתא true without saying that early ערלות counts.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading)
The fever left him

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is rejected. The sons in the ברייתא are a sick baby who got better, not a newborn. So the question about a baby too young for מילה is still open.

phrases.english: Rather, what are we dealing with here?
For example, where the fever left him.
phrases.notes: He was too sick for a ברית at slaughter time and got well before the eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading of the ברייתא after step 27 rejected the old one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sons were born between slaughter and eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son is a sick baby who recovered between slaughter and eating.

steps.title: A recovered baby should get seven days first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: שמואל says a baby who recovers from fever gets seven full days before מילה, so he would not be due by eating time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us give him all seven days! For שמואל said: if the fever left him, we give him all seven days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's new case using a rule of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fever left the baby only that day, he needs seven days to recover before his ברית. Then he still would not be fit for מילה at eating time, and the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A full seven days
We give him (time to recover)

phrases.english: But let us give him all seven days!
For שמואל said:
If the fever left him,
we give him all seven days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's case of a baby whose fever left him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under שמואל's rule, such a baby is not fit for מילה right away, so he should not hold back the eating.

steps.title: The seven days were already given
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the baby already finished his seven recovery days.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a case where we already gave him all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the seven days had already passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven days of recovery ended around ערב פסח. So by eating time the baby was fully fit for מילה, and רבא's case still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Where we already gave him

phrases.english: It is a case where we already gave him all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The baby just recovered and still needs seven days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seven days were already over.

steps.title: Then circumcise him in the morning
steps.stepSummary: If the seven days were over, the baby could have had his ברית that morning, before the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let him circumcise him in the morning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. If the baby was ready, why wasn't he circumcised in the morning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seven days were over by ערב פסח, the father could have done the ברית that morning, before the slaughter. Then the baby would not be a case of holding back only at eating time, and רבא's case falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: From the morning
Let him circumcise him

phrases.english: But let him circumcise him from the morning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 30.
